extracted.intended_audience: company officers, NCOs and infantry trainers responsible for preparing troops for night operations
extracted.subtask_description: A military field-manual style set of standards and practical criteria for training, preparing, and conducting infantry night marches, advances, and attacks; aimed at company-level officers and selected NCOs. Covers elementary instruction, reconnaissance, formations, protection, guidance, and assault/defensive procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic continuous training from depot
rubrics_metrics.description: Training for night operations must be systematic, progressive, and carried on continuously throughout the soldier’s whole service, beginning at the depot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elementary instruction should commence while the recruit is still at the depot; many units fail by only doing occasional night exercises. Continuous practice is essential to make night-fighting a normal part of soldier’s education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach recruits the different appearance of objects at night and the comparative visibility of men and objects under differing dress and backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: take men on ground they know, note visibility of khaki/tunic/shirt-sleeves, rising ground/sky-line effects, visibility of bright moving objects; test distance at which a struck match or man smoking can be seen; fire blank cartridges and teach recruits to judge rifle direction and approximate distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Train men to identify noises and estimate their approximate positions and to appreciate the penetrating power of the human voice; inculcate strict silence discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: men placed yards apart guess causes and positions of noises (mess tin rattle, bolt action, patrol movement). Practice sentry pairs with instructors crossing to teach watching in all directions. Emphasise that talking, even low voices, can be heard far and that silence is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding bearings at night
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach recruits to find and keep bearings by the pole star, other stars, landmarks or the wind, and recognise moon phases and whether the moon is rising or setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test: from a chosen spot 200+ paces away, have recruit take bearings while advancing, then be turned and ordered to continue on same line; teach checking direction by stars and landmarks, and returning by same means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moving in the dark (footwork and alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train small groups to march quietly and in step, lifting feet high, placing them down firmly & quietly, keeping touch with directing flank, conforming without sound or signal, turning into file for obstacles and reforming silently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with 3–4 recruits at close intervals, use visible mark or lamp for directing file, keep very slow pace with frequent halts to test collective movement. Obscure the guiding light intermittently; practice on rougher ground and longer lines with slower pace and more halts. After obstacles always halt to check alignment to avoid lateral drifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimising equipment noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Train each man to note parts of his equipment likely to cause noise (on lying down, rising, crossing obstacles) and take precautions to prevent sounds; always fix bayonets with scabbards on and carry rifles at proper angle to avoid clashing bayonets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early exercises without arms permitted, but progress to full marching order. Special attention to bayonet safety and rifle carriage to prevent accidental noise that betrays position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute prohibition on rifle fire during night attack
rubrics_metrics.description: Rifle-firing during a night attack is useless and may be 'absolutely criminal'; troops must be impressed not to fire and to rely on the bayonet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations state rifles not to be loaded, magazines charged and cut-offs closed—author prefers magazines not charged. Emphasise bayonet as the proper weapon and strict training against firing, smoking, striking matches, or talking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of night operations: march, advance, attack
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear definitions: night march = movement along roads/tracks in normal march formations; night advance = forward movement to gain ground for daylight progress, not to deliver decisive assault in darkness; night attack = delivered to gain possession of a locality held by enemy or to surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A night march may be prelude to an advance or attack but is considered ended upon arrival at assembly position. Use these definitions when planning and framing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough preparation and reconnaissance
rubrics_metrics.description: Success up to the moment of collision depends on the thoroughness of preparatory arrangements; obtain accurate information on ground and enemy positions by reconnoitring both by day and by night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detail too trivial; check positions for assembly and deployment that are easily identified at night and afford space; report positions and directions of obstacles; report extent and depth of enemy patrols. Reconnaissance reports by day must be verified by night visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan of operations maxims
rubrics_metrics.description: Maxims to bear in mind when preparing night plans: (1) quality, not number, counts; (2) the larger the force the greater the difficulty; (3) every detachment increases the risk of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple columns used, give each column a separate and distinct objective some distance apart. Maintain lateral communication (telephones recommended) so assaults may be simultaneous, but individual column commanders must press on if discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing and presentation of orders for night operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders (and the extracts to be read to troops at assembly) must be clearly and legibly typewritten because they may be read in very feeble light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare extracts limited to what troops need; ensure starting points allow the whole force to be drawn up before movement; detail a staff officer to verify unit presence and placement before march begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection during night operations: scouts and flanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection principles same as day but at night protecting bodies are smaller and closer; use scouts to give moving flank protection and avoid reliance on moving flanking piquets that leave the column disrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In night advances/attacks use lines of scouts at distances varying from 50 to 100 yards (per light). For close country on night marches, consider flanking piquets only if pre-positioned; otherwise scouts keep close to column for flank protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of connection between units
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining connection between portions of a force is of supreme importance because units can easily go astray in the dark and are hard to find.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to maintain lateral and rearward links; use connecting files within clear view where possible. Emphasise checks and halts to ensure units have not drifted or become disordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in planning but resolution in execution
rubrics_metrics.description: While weighing chances carefully before an offensive night operation is necessary, once commenced the undertaking must be carried through with utmost resolution; delay after discovery is disastrous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impress on all ranks that when the enemy opens fire the only course is to press on to the assault and decide the issue with the bayonet; hesitation hands precious seconds to defenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passive defence at night is useless
rubrics_metrics.description: Passive defence without impenetrable obstacles is suicidal at night; rifle fire is chance-dependent and cannot be relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defenders should deliver vigorous local counter-attacks with the bayonet from nearest bodies; do not wait to receive a charge—advance boldly; any local success must not be followed up unduly but used to buy time to reform under reserve protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction in reconnaissance for night operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Train officers, selected NCOs and men in reconnaissance by explaining the tactical scheme, letting them note ground by day, then criticise notes on the actual ground and repeat reconnaissance by night to compare reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initially allow free movement over ground; later mark hostile posts with flags and forbid approach. Always criticise reports on the ground; practise constantly in the dark to learn what points must be observed accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Night march formations and spacing (scouts, point, main guard, main body)
rubrics_metrics.description: In close country advanced guard consists of scouts, the point, and the main guard. Scouts start 2–3 minutes ahead of the point and keep in shadow; the point may be one section covering itself by a file ~30 paces ahead; main guard follows point 50–100 paces; main body follows at about double that distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scouts move quickly, halt at suspicious places to listen, and return warning if enemy discovered; they must not fire except to warn the column. Connecting files keep visual contact between elements; a company marching alone should also cover its rear with a few scouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in multiple night formations and rapid formation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must be practised to move at night in all possible formations (double and single rank), and to form rapidly into company/platoon/section single ranks to either flank or reform from file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice forming in single rank to either flank from file/single file. Keep about five paces between ranks in double rank. Keep force concentrated until deployment position reached; limit the number in front line and maintain reserves for eventualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding troops across country at night
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stars where visible; on very dark nights use assistants with luminous discs on chest and back, or pocket electric lamps to mark passage points through fences; in no-star conditions use slow method of marking fences and laying lines from posted assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistants face the guide and cover each other, moving from rear to front as column advances; expected advance rate ~1/2–3/4 mile per hour with trained assistants. In enclosed country send an officer and scouts with lamps to find gaps; if fences not parallel, halt, find and mark best passage and protect the company with scouts throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of the assault in night attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: If enemy opens fire after deployment, keep advancing until near enough to charge; do not reply to fire. Halt supporting lines to await developments; reserves must be retained and commander remain with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second/third lines act in prolongation of first line to envelop if needed, but avoid drawing reserves into the initial fight unless necessary. Upon success do not pursue; immediately form reserve to meet counter-attack and reform remainder under protection. Consider training for silent assault rather than cheering to avoid alerting neighbouring enemy supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silence and behaviour prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat and enforce warnings against firing, talking, striking matches, smoking, etc.; silence discipline must be strictly enforced in training so habits persist into war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field Service Regulations direct these warnings be explained before leaving assembly. Officers must not allow slackness; habits formed in peace will carry into war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and readiness of outposts
rubrics_metrics.description: Outposts receive the first brunt of night attacks; training in outpost duty must be thorough and taken seriously because neglect leads to being overwhelmed without timely warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice outpost duty under service conditions; do not habitually allow armistices at night in manoeuvres that prevent realistic training. Ensure outposts know how to give timely warnings and to execute local counter-attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicalities of scheduling night training
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary night exercises can generally be carried out before 10 p.m. (except mid-summer) and in short winter evenings immediately after tea; men should have recently eaten and be given soup/cocoa if kept out late or weather is cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with unarmed exercises and progress to full marching order; ensure men’s comfort and nutrition to maintain effectiveness during repeated night training sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting details for reconnaissance and assembly/deployment sites
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting ground, note that assembly/deployment spots must be easily identified at night and have sufficient space; record positions of obstacles and the direction they lie in; ascertain extent of enemy patrol penetration beyond advanced posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these additional details beyond the Field Service Regulations checklist; recognise that ground looks different at night and small surface features can disrupt formations if not reported and accounted for.
